summary: 70-year-old woman on day 4 after Hartmann's procedure: wound pain out of proportion, dusky skin spreading beyond the wound, grey "dishwater" discharge, crepitus; HR 126, T 38.4 °C, BP 92/60, lactate 4.1.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Wound pain and redness after operation
inputs.hpi: Day 4 after emergency Hartmann's procedure for perforated diverticulitis. Since this morning severe wound pain, far more than expected, with dusky skin spreading onto the flank over 6 hours and thin grey foul discharge from the wound. Rigors.

exam.abdomen: Midline wound: dusky grey skin edges, thin grey dishwater discharge, crepitus in the subcutaneous tissue extending 8 cm onto the left flank, tenderness beyond the erythema. Stoma pink.
exam.skin: Spreading dusky erythema from the wound onto the left flank, advancing over hours.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Necrotising fasciitis of the abdominal wall
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Post-operative necrotising soft-tissue infection of the laparotomy wound, day 4 after Hartmann's, with sepsis. Not a simple wound infection. Needs return to theatre for debridement.

mustRankTopK.note: Crepitus, dishwater discharge and pain out of proportion must lift NSTI above simple SSI.

mustNotMiss.note: Deep organ-space infection is the other post-laparotomy source.

redFlags.note: Penicillin allergy recorded: the regimen must account for it.

mustExclude.note: The documented plan must not be the superficial-SSI plan (open, oral co-amoxiclav, heal by secondary intention).

guideline.name: WSES/SIS-E consensus conference — management of skin and soft-tissue infections
guideline.section: Necrotising soft-tissue infections: clinical diagnosis (pain out of proportion, rapid progression, systemic toxicity); LRINEC has limited sensitivity and must not be used to rule out NSTI; prompt surgical debridement; empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics including an agent with anti-toxin activity (clindamycin) for streptococcal/clostridial infection; Fournier's gangrene
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Coccolini F, Kluger Y, et al. WSES/SIS-E consensus conference: recommendations for the management of skin and soft-tissue infections. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:58.

guideline.name: IDSA practice guideline — diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections (2014 update)
guideline.section: Purulent SSTI (abscess): incision and drainage; antibiotics active against MRSA when SIRS, immunocompromise or failed drainage; culture of abscess material. Non-purulent cellulitis: agent active against streptococci; severe: IV antibiotics and assess for necrotising infection. Necrotising infections: prompt surgical consultation, vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam (or carbapenem), clindamycin for toxin suppression in streptococcal NF
guideline.citation: Stevens DL, Bisno AL, Chambers HF, et al. Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections: 2014 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America. Clin Infect Dis. 2014;59:e10–52.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Septic shock / high likelihood of sepsis: blood cultures before antimicrobials, antimicrobials within 1 h, lactate, source control as soon as practical
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: post-operative NSTI of the laparotomy wound, easily mistaken for a superficial SSI. Tests the post-op context (isPostOp, wound CC template) against NSTI recognition, the penicillin-allergy flag and the documented plan.
